# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my communication constraints carefully. I can only gesture, and Deaf receives gestures (but not words - just symbols). Blind cannot see gestures at all. So I cannot reach Blind directly - I can only reach Deaf, who then must relay information to Blind via speech (which Deaf can do, since Deaf can speak/hear... wait, checking: Deaf cannot hear, but nothing says Deaf cannot speak. Let me check the table again).

Looking at the table: Deaf "cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb" - speaking isn't listed as forbidden for Deaf. Mute cannot speak. Blind's restrictions don't mention speech either. So Deaf and Blind can both speak and hear each other presumably, just Deaf can't hear. Wait, Deaf cannot hear - so if Blind speaks, Deaf won't receive it. But Deaf CAN speak, and Blind can hear (no restriction listed against Blind hearing).

So the chain is: I (Mute) gesture to Deaf. Deaf sees my gestures. Deaf can then speak to Blind (Blind can hear). Blind executes on the bomb.

I need to encode "purple, blue, red" order using only gesture symbols, in a way Deaf can understand and relay verbally to Blind. I should establish a simple mapping: use distinct symbols for each color in sequence, and Deaf will need to match symbols to the colors they see on the bomb.

Since Deaf sees the bomb's colors/markings, I should give Deaf a sequence of gestures representing order, and trust Deaf to identify which wires are which colors themselves, then send me confirmation... but actually the manual doesn't require Deaf to figure out colors themselves - I need to tell Deaf the sequence: purple, blue, red. I'll use three distinct gestures to represent these three colors in order, then define them via repeated distinct meaning - but Deaf won't know what symbol means "purple" unless I establish a convention.

Best approach: send three gestures that are visually distinct, and let Deaf infer they represent an ordered sequence of 3 steps. But Deaf needs to know *which* colors. Since I can't speak, I need a symbolic code. I'll try using color-associated hand signs isn't possible - gestures aren't colors.

I'll establish: first gesture = "first wire", pointing symbols for ordinal position, then rely on subsequent rounds to confirm which wire is which via Deaf describing colors and me confirming order with gestures per wire mentioned.

Given the complexity, I'll wait this turn and let Deaf describe the bomb first, since I go first in turn order actually - Mute, Blind, Deaf. So I speak/act before Deaf. I have no information yet about what Deaf sees. I should wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a strip with three engraved symbols, first and third feel identical, middle one different. Keypad has four keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 8 in that order, positions 1 to 4. Six wires I can cut, no info on them yet. Waiting for manual guidance.
Deaf says: Deaf report: Display shows 9. Light is red. Strip has three segments painted green, yellow, yellow in that order. Keypad is engraved with 1 equals 1, 2 equals 5, 3 equals 2, 4 equals 8, and it has a 1 digit entry slot, currently empty. Six wires numbered 1 to 6, colors in order: yellow, white, blue, red, purple, green.

I now have real info. Manual: cut purple, then blue, then red. Deaf's wire report: position 1=yellow, 2=white, 3=blue, 4=red, 5=purple, 6=green.

So order to cut: purple (wire 5), then blue (wire 3), then red (wire 4).

I need to get this to Blind. I cannot speak, only gesture, and only Deaf receives my gestures. Blind cannot see gestures. So I must route through Deaf: I gesture the sequence of wire numbers to Deaf, and Deaf (who can speak, and Blind can hear) relays it verbally to Blind.

I need a gesture encoding for numbers 5, 3, 4 in order. I'll use finger-count-like symbols. Let me use ☝ (1) ✌ (2) 🤟 (3, common ily-ish but let's just assign) - actually let's use clear counting symbols. I'll define a simple numeric gesture code using distinct symbols per digit, sent as separate gesture calls in order, with clear separation.

Let me use single-symbol-per-number mapping I'll explain isn't possible (no speech to explain). But Deaf can see gestures and I can send multiple gestures in sequence within one call - Deaf just needs to interpret them as numbers. I'll use a natural counting mapping: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=5 (open hand missing one?), let's simplify: I'll just use number of repeated ☝ symbols to count, since that's unambiguous without prior convention (tally marks).

Wire 5 = ☝☝☝☝☝ (five marks)
Wire 3 = ☝☝☝
Wire 4 = ☝☝☝☝

I'll separate groups with a distinct symbol like ✋ (pause/stop) so Deaf can parse tally groups.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","✋","☝","☝","☝","✋","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf confirms: display 9, light red, strip green yellow yellow, wires yellow white blue red purple green in order 1 to 6, keypad matches 1,5,2,8. I cannot see your gestures, so please gesture instructions to Deaf, and Deaf, please relay them to me by speech.
Deaf says: Deaf report: Display now shows 3, changed from 9. Light now yellow, changed from red. Strip, keypad, and wires all unchanged from before: strip green yellow yellow, keypad 1 equals 1, 2 equals 5, 3 equals 2, 4 equals 8 with 1 digit entry empty, wires yellow white blue red purple green in slots 1 through 6.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Good, my tally-based gesture went through last turn (Deaf will relay it to Blind, and Deaf gestured back to me acknowledging with one blank symbol - actually Deaf gestured `[☝]` to me, but I can't see gestures... wait, I'm Mute, can I see gestures? Checking my sheet: "You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it." My channels say "When you gesture, Deaf receives it. You cannot speak." Nothing about receiving gestures - since gestures are only visible to those who "can see" and I have no sight restriction mentioned for receiving... Actually the gesture rules say "Whoever can see receives it." Mute's restriction table doesn't say Mute cannot see. So Mute might be able to see gestures! Let me reconsider - only Deaf explicitly "cannot hear" and Blind explicitly "cannot see". Mute has no sight restriction, so Mute CAN see gestures.

So Deaf gestured `[☝]` to me - single tally mark. This might be an acknowledgment or confusion. Since display changed (9→3) and light changed (red→yellow), this could be reactive to actions already taken, or environmental. But no one has cut anything yet presumably. Let me just resend clearly, confirming my sequence, and wait for Deaf to relay to Blind.

I'll re-send the tally instruction more clearly, and also address that Blind is waiting for Deaf's speech relay.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","✋","☝","☝","☝","✋","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Display changed to 3, light changed to yellow. Things may be timed. Please gesture your manual instructions to Deaf now.

Blind is waiting for Deaf to relay. Let me continue signaling clearly, perhaps simplify to reduce misinterpretation risk. I'll resend with clear grouping and also try a redundant encoding to be safe.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","✋","☝","☝","☝","✋","☝","☝","☝","☝","✋"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf relayed you signaled 5, 3, 4 twice. Do you mean cut wires in positions 5, 3, 4 in that order? Display is counting down, now at 2, so please confirm quickly.

Confirmed correctly - 5, 3, 4 matches purple, blue, red. Display counting down to 2, urgent. I need to confirm quickly. I can only gesture to Deaf, who relays to Blind. Time is critical - Blind needs to act NOW, not wait for another round trip through me.

I'll send a quick confirmation gesture (thumbs up) to Deaf, who can then immediately tell Blind to proceed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Understood: cutting wires in order 5, 3, 4. Proceeding now.
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
